core_obligations: Construct the approximating system: triples (a, b, f) with finite-presentation middle terms; morphisms of triples; the index category is directed.

Cofinality: every object admits a map from a triple, and the two characterizations (of morphisms of triples via the proposition) compose correctly; the Categories cofinal lemma then identifies the colimit.
Conclusion: the given morphism is the limit of its finite-presentation approximations.
proof_roadmap: Define triples and their morphisms; directedness.
Cofinality via the characterization proposition twice.
Colimit identification via the Categories lemma.
difficulty_reason: Triple (a, b, f) cofinal system construction with two applications of the characterization proposition and the Categories initial/cofinal lemma; the cofinality verification is real work.

compared.difference: The sibling constrains the approximation to preserve relative dimension; this lemma is the unconstrained approximation machinery. Different statements; the sibling builds on this one's architecture.
